The map's label, in 1200, for the Berber (Amazigh) tribes of the western Sahara and its edges, from the Atlantic coast inland to the Niger bend, outside the direct rule of any state.

Berbers are the native peoples of North Africa. Around 1200 most lived in tribes grouped into large confederations. The Masmuda farmed the Atlas Mountains and had just built the Almohad Caliphate. The Sanhaja herded camels in the desert; a century earlier one of their branches had founded the Almoravid state (see Almoravids and Almohads). The Zenata lived on the steppes and would soon found new kingdoms such as the Marinids.

The desert tribes on this part of the map lived by herding, raiding and guiding caravans. They carried salt south and gold north on the trans-Saharan routes linking the Maghreb with Ghana and, soon, the Mali Empire. Their conversion to Islam helped carry the faith into West Africa.
